ov: Sea bivalves found in every ocean but never in fresh water. Unlike most bivalves, many are free-living and swim in short bursts, clapping their shells to jet away from predators such as starfish. A ring of tiny eyes lines the edge of the body inside the shell.

why.et: Highly prized as seafood, and some species are farmed; the part usually sold as "scallop" is the big adductor muscle.

rg: All the world's oceans; never in fresh water.
fx: Its eyes focus light with curved mirrors made of guanine crystals instead of a lens.
Young scallops drift in the plankton, then settle and often anchor themselves with a thread.
